papers.title: Embedded sensing telemetry and a validated explicit finite element digital twin of pressurised uPVC pipe under low velocity impact
papers.abstract: Polymeric pipelines are increasingly used for pressurized fluid transport, yet their behavior under accidental low-velocity impact, and the means to monitor it in service, remain underdeveloped relative to metallic systems. This study recasts a combined experimental and numerical investigation of clamped unplasticized poly(vinyl chloride) (uPVC) pipe as the first building block of a physics-based digital twin for polymeric utility pipelines. A drop-weight rig was instrumented with a purpose-built ESP32-S2 sensing unit, using infrared timing gates and a pressure transducer, that streams real impact telemetry: the hammer velocity and the transient internal pressure pulse. Five water-pressurized specimens, spanning 689.48 to 2068.43 kPa, were struck at mid-span by a 4 kg hammer at 5.56 m/s, and a high-fidelity ABAQUS/Explicit counterpart was synchronized against the measured response. As internal pressure rose, the peak contact force increased from 3527 to 4174 N, the permanent deformation fell from 15.1 to 7.0 mm, and the pressure pulse grew while the contact period shortened, all consistent with pressure-induced wall stiffening. The contact-force response was linear up to about 1379 kPa before plateauing at the onset of the burst-pressure regime. Experimental and numerical plastic-zone areas agreed to within 16.9%, a conservative over-prediction the twin corrects during synchronization. On this validated basis, a conceptual digital-twin framework is proposed, enabling real-time damage identification and predictive, surrogate-driven structural health monitoring of polymeric pipelines.

papers.title: STEM faculty perception of student resistance as a source of faculty's self‐efficacy
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Despite decades of reform efforts, lecture remains the dominant mode of instruction in undergraduate engineering education. Faculty often cite student resistance to active learning as a barrier to instructional change. However, little research has examined how faculty perceptions of such resistance influence their motivation and instructional practices. Purpose/Hypothesis(es) Guided by Social Cognitive Theory, this study investigates how faculty perceptions and students' self‐reported resistance influence faculty self‐efficacy and the adoption of active learning instructional practices. Design/Method This longitudinal study involved 173 STEM faculty and 1649 students across 64 U.S. institutions. Faculty completed surveys at three time points over two terms; students completed surveys at the middle time point after an active learning session. Latent change score modeling was used to examine the relations between faculty self‐efficacy, instructional practice, and resistance. Results Faculty self‐efficacy at the start of the semester predicted increased use of active learning. Faculty perceptions of student resistance partially mediated this relation, while student‐reported resistance did not. Students' self‐reported resistance was higher in engineering than in other disciplines. Overall, faculty perceptions of student resistance were only weakly related to student reports; however, this relation may be much stronger within engineering courses. Conclusions Faculty self‐efficacy for approaches to teaching that focus on active learning and perceptions of student resistance to active learning play a significant role in shaping instructional practices. To support a broader adoption of active learning in engineering education, professional development should target self‐efficacy for using active learning and strategies to reduce student resistance.

papers.title: Evolution‐Inspired Multi‐Objective Bayesian Optimization for Protein Engineering
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Protein engineering requires efficient navigation of vast sequence spaces under limited evaluation budgets, especially when multiple properties must be optimized simultaneously. We developed evolution‐inspired multi‐objective Bayesian optimization (EvoMOBO), an active‐learning framework that integrates path‐dependent sequence generation, global candidate competition, and explicit multi‐objective optimization, enabling efficient prioritization of high‐value variants without exhaustive library enumeration. Compared with state‐of‐the‐art methods on complete steroid receptor DNA‐binding domain (DBD) and ParD3 antitoxin landscapes, EvoMOBO achieved greater target‐region enrichment while maintaining sequence diversity across two‐ and three‐objective tasks. In the DBD landscape, optimization guided by simulation‐derived geometric descriptors enriched variants with satisfactory experimental performance without experimental labels. Building on this validation, we applied EvoMOBO to two enzyme‐engineering tasks using mechanistic descriptors, with experiments reserved for final validation. For an old yellow enzyme from Geobacillus kaustophilus , probabilities of substrate binding and reaction preorganization guided optimization of a non‐native oxidative dehydrogenation, yielding a variant that increased substrate conversion from 17.5% to 95%. For a formate oxidase from Aspergillus oryzae , stability‐related descriptors identified aggregation‐resistant variants that nearly doubled diethyl phthalate degradation in a photoenzymatic cascade. Together, these results demonstrate robust multi‐objective optimization by EvoMOBO and show that mechanism‐derived descriptors can effectively guide protein engineering toward experimentally improved functions.

papers.title: Le scuole sperimentali italiane e il modello giapponese di Tomoe Gakuen: un confronto pedagogico tra educazione attiva, personalizzazione e comunità educante
papers.abstract: This article examines comparatively the main Italian experimental and alternative educational models — including Montessori education, Reggio Emilia approach, Waldorf/Steiner schools, and other active learning experiences — in relation to the Japanese educational experience of Tomoe Gakuen, founded by Sōsaku Kobayashi in the 1930s. The study aims to identify pedagogical convergences and divergences concerning the concepts of child-centered education, experiential learning, educational freedom, personalization, relational pedagogy, and the role of the educational environment. Through a historical-comparative and pedagogical analysis, the paper highlights how Tomoe Gakuen represented an innovative educational experience within the Japanese context, anticipating several contemporary educational themes such as inclusion, holistic development, emotional well-being, interdisciplinarity, and community-based education. The article also investigates the different epistemological foundations underlying these educational models: scientific pedagogy in Montessori education, socio-constructivist and democratic perspectives in the Reggio Emilia approach, spiritual-anthroposophical principles in Waldorf education, and the humanistic-experiential orientation characterizing Tomoe Gakuen. The comparative framework demonstrates that, despite cultural and historical differences, these educational experiences share a common critique of traditional authoritarian schooling and promote an integral vision of human development centered on the dignity, autonomy, and uniqueness of the child. Finally, the study reflects on the contemporary relevance of these pedagogical paradigms in addressing current educational challenges related to standardization, student well-being, and inclusive schooling.

papers.title: Impact of Heat‐Treatment‐Induced Microstructural Evolution on the High‐Temperature Wear and Corrosion Resistance of L‐PBF Scalmalloy
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT The high‐temperature (HT) tribological and corrosion performance of Scalmalloy produced via laser powder bed fusion (L‐PBF) remains insufficiently uncharacterized despite its growing adoption in many industrial applications. This study examines the impact of post‐heat treatment (325°C for 4 h) on the microstructure, nano‐hardness, room‐temperature (RT) and HT tribological behavior and corrosion resistance of the alloy. Microstructural characterization revealed that heat treatment conserved the bimodal microstructure achieved in the L‐PBF process, while improving the homogenous distribution of coherent Al 3 (Sc,Zr) nanoprecipitates, as evidenced by x‐ray diffraction analysis. The coherent nanoparticles restricted the localized plastic deformation by inhibiting the movement of dislocations, thus enhancing the nano‐hardness. The refined precipitate distribution enhanced the nano‐indentation hardness from 3.50 ± 0.10 to 4.26 ± 0.11 GPa, resulting in an improved wear resistance. During reciprocating sliding, the Post‐Heat‐Treated (PHT) Scalmalloy exhibited lower friction coefficient, wear volume loss, and specific wear rate compared to that of As‐Printed (ASP) alloy. With 200°C test temperature, the wear rate was dropped to 39.23%, which was due to the precipitation of Al 3 (Sc,Zr) and the formation of an oxide tribo‐layer. Corrosion resistance was also superior, with the PHT specimen achieving a corrosion rate of 0.3809 mpy at RT and lower weight loss under HT corrosion compared to the ASP condition.

papers.title: Hybrid Mathematical-PINN Model for Tumor-Immune Interaction with Holling Type-II Functional Response and Optimal Control
papers.abstract: Code accompanying the article “Hybrid Mathematical-PINN Model for Tumor-Immune Interaction with Holling Type-II Functional Response and Optimal Control”. The package reproduces the dynamical-systems results for the three-variable tumor, hunting-cell and resting-cell model with Holling Type-II responses and tumor-induced immune suppression (baseline parameters of Table 2, μd = 0.05). It contains the RK4 reference solution; the exact analysis of the interior equilibria, including the quintic coexistence condition, the saddle-node bifurcation near w2 = 0.4385 and a count of admissible equilibria over the parameter ranges studied; the Sotomayor conditions for the transcritical bifurcation of the hunting-cell-free equilibrium; the Hopf point and first Lyapunov coefficient; and the regenerated bifurcation diagram (Figure 4) with its limit-cycle envelope. A verification folder holds independent re-implementations of a forward–backward sweep for the Pontryagin optimal-control problem and of a state-only physics-informed neural network, with analytic gradients checked against finite differences. [Scripts used for Figures 1–3 and 5–9 and Table 6 are in the folder.] This version updates the earlier deposit to match the revised article. The code is written in Python (NumPy, SciPy, SymPy, mpmath, Matplotlib); the README gives the run order, expected outputs and run times.

papers.title: A Physical Testbed for Self-Driving Laboratories: Comparing Bayesian and Agentic Optimization in a Minimal Closed-Loop Color Formulation Task
papers.abstract: Self-driving laboratories (SDLs) integrate laboratory robotics and automation with AI-driven decision-making to close the design-build-test-learn (DBTL) cycle. However, physical testbeds that combine off-the-shelf hardware and AI into a functioning closed-loop workflow remain in early stages of development, and their integration with commercial laboratory automation is comparatively less developed. In this work, we develop a physical testbed that assembles and integrates commercially available laboratory automation instruments and demonstrate continuous, closed-loop, autonomous operation over 24 cumulative hours of unattended experimentation. We validate this platform on a minimal closed-loop discovery task in which the system autonomously formulates aqueous dye mixtures to match a target absorbance spectrum. The system completed six independent campaigns, each consisting of 48 closed-loop iterations over approximately four hours. In every campaign, the system autonomously selected, dispensed, and measured each mixture, with an AI-driven decision-making algorithm determining subsequent formulations without human intervention. Using this testbed, we compared the performance of two AI-driven decision-making algorithms, traditional Bayesian optimization (BO) and an agentic approach, in selecting mixtures under a fixed total-volume constraint. The agentic optimizer matched target absorbance spectra using fewer iterations than BO, with reductions up to 52%, and converged on a solution for one target that BO failed to match within 48 iterations. These results demonstrate a reference physical platform for SDLs that can evaluate both established and emerging AI strategies, including large language model (LLM)-directed optimization, before their deployment in real-world applications where experiments may be costly and time-consuming to prepare.

papers.title: HINT-VLM: Humanoid Interactive Navigation over Rough Terrain with Embodiment-Grounded Vision-Language Model
papers.abstract: Humanoid robots have achieved significant progress in locomotion and manipulation, enabling traversal over rough terrain and richer interaction with the environment, such as moving obstacles. However, most traditional navigation methods assume non-interactive environments and focus only on traversal. While Navigation Among Movable Obstacles (NAMO) approaches relax this assumption, prior efforts have largely focused on flat environments and reactive interaction, rather than predicting object movability and planning ahead. These limitations become critical in outdoor rough-terrain scenarios, where robots must jointly reason about terrain traversability and object movability. In this work, we address NAMO for humanoid robots in cluttered outdoor rough terrain by proposing a hybrid planning framework that combines semantic priors from a Vision-Language Model (VLM) with embodied robot interaction data through a Gaussian process (GP) residual model. The GP corrects the VLM-derived movability prior to produce embodiment-grounded probabilistic movability estimates, which are then incorporated into hierarchical uncertainty-aware planning. The proposed approach allows humanoids to jointly leverage locomotion and manipulation for efficient and safe navigation, representing the first solution to NAMO in rough terrain through predictive movability reasoning and probabilistic VLM integration.

papers.title: Feel My Focus: Gaze-Triggered Digital Twin Creation for Remote Collaboration
papers.abstract: We present Feel My Focus, a gaze-triggered mixed reality (MR) demonstration that enables rapid creation and sharing of lightweight 3D digital twins during remote collaboration. Unlike systems that use gaze primarily as a referential pointer, Feel My Focus treats sustained visual attention as a generative action: a fixation on a physical object initiates single-image capture, attention-guided segmentation, and one-shot 3D reconstruction, allowing a remote partner to inspect and discuss the object in situ. The system integrates gaze-tracking glasses, modular segmentation and reconstruction services, and an MR client for runtime streaming and interaction. This design prioritizes responsiveness and experiential continuity over photometric fidelity. We report observations from a public demonstration, highlighting design trade-offs, failure modes, and user control considerations for deploying gaze-triggered generative systems in real-world collaborative settings.

papers.abstract: Organizing control around events can reduce sensing and actuation demands while directly linking control decisions to the occurrence and timing of desired system behaviors. This paper proposes a novel event-centric model predictive control (MPC) framework that unifies event sensing, event prediction, and event regulation. Events define the feedback information, prediction horizon, and event-timing objectives, placing them at the center of predictive control design. The framework is developed for a scanning mirror system equipped with a baseline neuromorphic controller composed of spiking neurons that supports sparse actuation. The control objective is to achieve prescribed zero-crossing times and a desired scanning range while minimizing the mechanical energy transferred between the actuator and the mirror. A sampling-based algorithm is presented to obtain suboptimal solutions of the event-centric MPC optimization problem without requiring an explicit event-to-event prediction model. By grounding predictive optimization in events, the proposed framework opens a new direction for MPC design and its integration with neuromorphic control.

papers.title: ScanDreamer: A Map-Grounded World Model for Quadrotor Navigation
papers.abstract: Quadrotors inspecting buildings and tunnels must navigate unknown clutter with a forward-facing depth camera whose limited field of view constrains scene understanding and collision-avoiding navigation. Recent world-model agents learn navigation through imagined experience (e.g., AirDreamer), but remain data-intensive and often lack explicit geometric memory and awareness of what the camera can observe. We propose ScanDreamer, a map-grounded world model that constructs an online 2D scan-memory map from depth images and vehicle pose. Our world model, actor, and critic are conditioned on this map, which also defines a geodesic progress reward. Moreover, a forward-cone penalty discourages horizontal motion outside the camera's viewing direction. During imagination, ScanDreamer propagates the quadrotor pose over a frozen map and derives progress and wall-contact signals from the mapped geometry. We train ScanDreamer for 0.8 million environment steps (5.5 h on one GPU) and evaluate it in NVIDIA Isaac Sim over 1560 episodes spanning unseen layouts and parameter ranges. Across three seeds (mean $\pm$ SD), ScanDreamer achieves 96.3 $\pm$ 0.3% success with 3.6 $\pm$ 0.3% collision, compared with 59.6 $\pm$ 3.0% success and 28.8 $\pm$ 2.8% collision for AirDreamer at the same online-interaction budget. Removing the forward-cone penalty increases collisions to 9.9 $\pm$ 3.1%. These results show that combining explicit map memory, map-grounded imagination, and perception-aware motion substantially improves navigation performance and data efficiency. The source code is available at https://github.com/WANGSHUAIzzzz/ScanDreamer.

papers.title: Robust Gaussian process regression: posterior contraction
papers.abstract: Gaussian processes form a popular and flexible class of prior distributions with principled uncertainty quantification, but the Gaussian likelihood on which the corresponding posterior relies makes them highly sensitive to outliers and contaminated observations. We study Gaussian process regression when among the $n$ observations, $m$ of these are possibly contaminated. A generic framework to obtain posterior contraction rates in this setting is considered, from a frequentist perspective as the sample size $n$ and the number of corrupted observations $m$ grow. We adopt a generalized Bayes approach in which the log--likelihood is replaced by a robustified version; we discuss various choices thereof, such as one recently proposed by Altamirano et al. that preserves conjugacy. We investigate the minimax rate of estimation under adversarial contamination in terms of the Sobolev smoothness $β$ of the regression function and $m$. The question of building adaptive procedures to both $β$ and $m$ is investigated, and we show that a polynomial loss for adaptation must be paid in general. We instantiate our results for Matérn Gaussian process and deep ReLU network priors. Numerical experiments for existing and new robust algorithms are provided, illustrating the practical applicability of our results.

papers.title: K-PWM: Control-Oriented Structured Bilinear World Models under Partial Observation
papers.abstract: World models learn internal simulators of environment dynamics for prediction, planning, and control, yet learning them from limited, noisy, and partial observations remains challenging. While much progress has focused on pixel-based observations, many physical systems instead provide vector-valued measurements that reveal only part of the underlying state. We introduce K-PWM, a probabilistic world model for prediction and control under partial observation. K-PWM couples Koopman-bilinear latent dynamics with a nonlinear observation decoder and performs probabilistic latent-state inference through the learned model via extended Kalman filtering and smoothing, without a separately trained inference network. Its bilinear structure enables exact propagation of the maintained Gaussian belief through the latent transition and efficient rollouts for uncertainty-aware model predictive path integral (MPPI) control. For training K-PWM, we present a generalized expectation conditional maximization (GECM) procedure with closed-form updates for the generators, noise covariances, and latent prior, complemented by gradient-based decoder learning. A Koopman-consistent initialization selects the latent dimension from data and initializes the action-dependent dynamics. With limited training data, K-PWM achieves lower long-horizon prediction error than the evaluated baselines on partially observed Gymnasium MuJoCo systems, while substantially reducing training time relative to the strongest prediction baseline. On high-dimensional MuJoCo Menagerie robots, it achieves competitive tracking accuracy with low per-step computation times, demonstrating potential for real-time deployment. These results support structured probabilistic dynamics as a data- and compute-efficient approach to world modeling and control under partial observation.

papers.title: Breaking survivorship bias in driving world models
papers.abstract: World models allow autonomous vehicles to imagine the consequences of candidate actions before execution, but their reliability depends on the futures represented in their training data. We identify a survivorship bias in driving world models: because the futures recorded in prevailing driving datasets almost always end safely, existing models often imagine benign outcomes even when a collision is imminent. We introduce a neutral world model (NWM) that learns both routine and safety-critical futures from a mixture of routine driving and real accident videos with a bounding-box-guided objective. The NWM more faithfully anticipates imminent collisions, while maintaining a low false collision rate and competitive generation quality in routine driving. We further use the model as an imagination engine for decision-making. Given multiple ego trajectories, the NWM predicts the future associated with each candidate, and a reward function evaluates these imagined outcomes before selecting an action. On challenging NAVSIM scenarios, this procedure selects the better trajectory more reliably than the baseline world model. Zero-shot experiments with real-world pedestrian dummy crossing data collected using an autonomous research vehicle further demonstrate transfer to unseen sensor observations. These results show that correcting survivorship bias enables world models to more faithfully reason about futures and support safety-critical decision-making in autonomous driving.

papers.title: ForeAct: Geometry-Guided Action Learning from World Representations
papers.abstract: Robotic manipulation requires representations that capture both scene geometry and its evolution during interaction. Existing approaches have largely treated these two aspects separately. World action models capture such dynamics by coupling action prediction with future video generation, but their reliance on iterative diffusion or rectified-flow inference leads to high computational cost, while their representations lack explicit spatial structure. Explicitly modeling scene geometry typically requires auxiliary modules that increase both parameter count and computational cost. Conversely, geometry-centric policies primarily recover observed spatial structure and often lack explicit supervision for anticipating future geometric changes during interaction. To address these limitations, we introduce ForeAct, which repurposes a pretrained video world model as a single-pass representation backbone for low-latency control. ForeAct directly processes the clean latent of the current observation in one forward pass, eliminating future-frame synthesis and iterative denoising while retaining the backbone's pretrained spatiotemporal priors. Rather than introducing a separate geometry backbone, ForeAct uses learnable tokens supervised by next-frame relative depth to shape the shared video representation through bidirectional self-attention. This compact interface turns the spatial knowledge already encoded in the backbone into a future-aware representation for action generation, with little parameter overhead. The lightweight geometry readout is used only during training and removed at deployment, enabling low-latency, geometry-aware control without depth input or an external geometry backbone. Without additional large-scale pretraining, ForeAct achieves 96.6% average success on LIBERO, 63.5% on SimplerEnv-Bridge, and a 74.4% success rate across 90 real-world rollouts.

papers.title: Does Predictive Performance Translate to Causal Performance? Evaluating tabular foundation models as nuisance learners for causal effect estimation
papers.abstract: Tabular foundation models based on prior-data fitted networks (PFNs) achieve strong predictive performance, but their value for causal inference is unclear. We evaluated whether PFNs, which predict through in-context learning, could match or outperform conventional nuisance learners in supporting accurate causal estimation and reliable uncertainty quantification (inference). Learners modeled propensity scores and outcome regressions within doubly robust estimators of average causal effects, with and without cross-fitting, across synthetic and semi-synthetic settings with varying confounding complexity and effect heterogeneity.   Under simple parametric data-generating processes, the PFNs were competitive with correctly specified parametric regressions and ensembles containing them. In more complex settings, they outperformed all conventional learners evaluated, including richly specified Super Learner ensembles, for both accuracy and uncertainty quantification. As sample size increased, only the two PFN models (TabPFN and Mitra) consistently approached nominal confidence interval coverage, whereas under-coverage persisted for conventional learners. In some settings, PFNs achieved near-nominal coverage and well-calibrated standard errors even without cross-fitting. At the smallest sample size (n=200) and in the higher-dimensional semi-synthetic settings, PFNs and other flexible learners exhibited poor coverage without cross-fitting. For PFNs, this appeared to be driven by propensity score overfitting consistent with in-sample memorization of treatment labels. These findings highlight the promise of prior-data fitted networks as in-context nuisance learners for causal estimation, while underscoring the need for further evaluation in challenging settings.

papers.title: ALETHEIA: A Multi-Frequency Eddy Current Pulsed Thermography Dataset for Neural Operator Learning in Nondestructive Testing
papers.abstract: Learning neural solvers for spatiotemporal partial differential equations (PDEs) under real-world constraints remains a key challenge in scientific machine learning, especially for inverse tasks with sparse and noisy boundary observations. We present the Aletheia dataset, the first 3D benchmark for learning data-driven solvers in the context of nondestructive testing (NDT). The dataset simulates eddy-current-induced heating in conductive solids and models the resulting transient heat propagation governed by the heat equation. Aletheia contains over 4,700 high-resolution samples across 10 excitation frequencies (1-100,kHz), each providing volumetric heat source and temperature fields over time. It supports both forward prediction of temperature evolution and inverse reconstruction of internal heat sources or defects from surface infrared measurements. Real infrared thermography data from cracked rail specimens are included for calibration and comparison. We define four canonical tasks on both regular and irregular grids and benchmark them using various neural operators. Aletheia establishes a unified platform for evaluating neural PDE solvers under realistic NDT conditions, enabling progress in reliable, data-driven inverse modeling. The dataset and code are publicly available at https://github.com/sherlock-0327/ALETHEIA.

papers.title: DeepSoMo: Deformable Object Motion Estimation under Proprioceptive Partial Observability via Predictive Latent Dynamics
papers.abstract: Estimating the motion of deformable bodies in soft robotics from proprioceptive sensing is challenging due to partial observability, as internal observations provide only indirect access to global motion, contact, and shape evolution. In such settings, instantaneous observations are insufficient, and accurate estimation requires temporally consistent latent representations. This paper studies deformable motion estimation under proprioceptive partial observability from a latent dynamics perspective. We argue that a key requirement for long-horizon estimation is latent temporal consistency, where latent states remain predictive of future observations. To this end, we present DeepSoMo, a learning-based framework that enforces predictive structure in latent dynamics through a self-supervised latent prediction constraint. We evaluate the approach in a canonical deformable dynamics setting using high-fidelity finite-element simulation as a controlled source of ground truth. Results demonstrate consistent improvements in trajectory estimation, orientation recovery, shape reconstruction, and contact inference over architecture-matched recurrent baselines.

papers.title: EbbFlow: PINN-Inspired Progressive Curriculum for MeanFlow Training
papers.abstract: MeanFlow learns interval-average velocity for few-step generation, but its fixed temporal sampler mixes diagonal and interior supervision throughout training. We interpret temporal coordinates as collocation points: diagonal samples provide a stochastic boundary target, whereas finite intervals supply a differential-consistency target. The diagonal fraction controls how often the consistency component appears, while interval length enters its gradient through an explicit factor. Motivated by this distinction, EbbFlow uses Temporal Supervision Allocation (TSA) to schedule the diagonal fraction and interval geometry. It starts with diagonal supervision, then admits interior samples and expands their maximum interval; a left-anchored interval law preserves coverage across time. The per-sample loss, target, backbone, and inference procedure remain unchanged. In matched class-conditional ImageNet $256\times 256$ runs without classifier-free guidance (DiT-B/2, one training seed per method, 400k updates), EbbFlow achieves 50k-sample FID of 39.65 at one network evaluation and 36.02 at two-evaluation ODE sampling, versus 44.82 and 39.86 for MeanFlow. Gradient probes show a mid-training difference in component geometry. Ablations support allocation scheduling and left-anchored intervals, although a fixed full-horizon variant performs better at one evaluation. These results suggest that temporal sampling is a useful training control whose benefits depend on the inference protocol.

papers.title: DexForesight: Grounding Dexterous Policies with Implicit Spatial Foresight
papers.abstract: Dexterous manipulation requires rich spatial foresight over both the surrounding scene and the robot hand. Existing world-action models often acquire such predictive knowledge through explicit future prediction. We introduce DexForesight, a framework that learns spatial foresight implicitly by injecting dynamics-aware world representations into the latent space of a dexterous policy. During training, DexForesight learns an action-conditioned spatial world model from offline scene depth, kinematic hand geometry, and demonstration trajectories. The world model predicts 3D hand-point motion and visual feature changes, capturing both articulated hand dynamics and scene changes under demonstrated actions, including the motion of fingers occluded from the cameras. We then freeze the world model and align policy queries with its predictive world queries, transferring the learned spatial dynamics into policy latents and using them to condition action generation. At deployment, only the policy is retained, operating on RGB observations, language, and robot state without depth input or explicit future prediction. On 11 DexJoCo simulation tasks, DexForesight improves the overall success rate of the base policy from 49.4% to 60.5%. On three real-robot dexterous manipulation tasks, DexForesight achieves 58.3% success, compared with 50.0% for the strongest baseline.Project page https://dexforesight.github.io/

papers.title: SurgWorld: Learning Surgical Representations Beyond Observation via Latent Prediction
papers.abstract: Surgical procedures are inherently partially observable, requiring surgeons to continuously infer evolving anatomical dynamics and future surgical states beyond the current observation. However, existing self-supervised learning methods primarily learn from observed surgical videos through masked reconstruction or predicting representations within the camera's current field of view, lacking the capability to explicitly model the out-of-sight surgical dynamics. Inspired by latent predictive world models, we introduce SurgWorld, a video-native, self-supervised framework for surgical representation learning, which treats a specified spatial or temporal shift as a pseudo-action and learns to predict the target latent representation from a partial observation. Specifically, we propose Out-of-Sight Dynamics Modeling (OSDM) as the pretraining objective for predicting representations conditioned on relative spatio-temporal shifts. We further regularize the learned latent dynamics from OSDM with a Geometric Visual Similarity (GVS) objective by aligning patch-level relational structures between predicted and target representations, preserving spatial geometry and local visual coherence for dense perception. These two objectives are integrated through an agglomerative training framework that consolidates complementary supervisory signals from multiple teachers to learn a unified latent representation of surgical dynamics and visual geometry. Extensive transfer learning experiments on 17 surgical benchmarks show that SurgWorld consistently outperforms existing vision foundation models across surgical workflow recognition, fine-grained action understanding, and dense visual perception. We further conduct tailored qualitative and quantitative analyses, demonstrating that SurgWorld effectively captures surgical dynamics beyond the directly observed context through latent prediction.

The pipeline combines human mesh recovery, kinematic retargeting, reinforcement learning for motion tracking in simulation, and onboard deployment via ONNX. Training ran on a single RTX 5070 GPU. An eleven-version deployment ladder evaluated on hardware examines three interventions. We detect and repair silent corruption of deployment artifacts, model state-estimator drift during training, and edit the reference motion to support stable execution and a controlled ending. The final policies achieved three consecutive rope-free completions of a 43-second routine, a 46-second performance with automatic handoff, and a continuous 9.7-minute rope-free performance composed from the captured motion. In a live handover, a single remote request let the robot start from and return to the manufacturer's walking controller on stage, with a measured torque-free window of 45-140 ms. We report the training dynamics and hardware outcomes and discuss failure boundaries involving compliant flooring and occlusion in monocular capture.

papers.title: Dual Model Predictive Control through Sampling-Based Belief Propagation
papers.abstract: We propose a sampling-based dual model predictive control (MPC) approach that combines belief propagation with parameterized feedback policy optimization. By sampling uncertain dynamics and process noise, we approximate the evolution of the hyperstate over the prediction horizon, allowing future control decisions to adapt to anticipated observations and belief updates. This enables the controller to account for the future value of information without explicit exploration incentives. We establish almost-sure uniform convergence of the sample-average objective to the finite-horizon expected objective over a compact policy class. The approach is specialized to Bayesian linear regression and evaluated on stochastic systems with constant and time-varying uncertain dynamics. We compare our approach to certainty equivalent control, and an MPC that optimizes over open-loop control sequences rather than feedback policies, demonstrating the benefits of our method in terms of both control performance and information gain.

papers.title: ObjectWorld: Scaling Object-Centric World Models with A Large-Scale 3D Full-Object Flow Dataset
papers.abstract: Generative world modeling from large-scale visual data offers a promising path toward scalable robot manipulation. This calls for an intermediate representation that can be supervised at scale and remains actionable for downstream control. We propose 3D full-object flow, an object-centric motion representation that assigns dense 3D trajectories to points across the complete surface of a target object, including its occluded regions. By extending visible-surface object flow to the full object geometry, this representation makes complete object motion explicit and applies uniformly to both rigid and deformable objects. To realize the potential of this representation at scale, we introduce a 1210-hour full-object flow dataset that addresses the scarcity of large-scale supervision for complete 3D object motion. The dataset integrates diverse real-world videos and physical simulations, with a scalable annotation pipeline for recovering full-object motion from real-world observations and quality metrics for systematically assessing annotation quality. We then train a world model that takes an image and a task description as input and predicts dense full-object flow over the reconstructed object geometry. Experiments show reliable annotation quality, data-scalable flow prediction, and effective downstream manipulation across novel scenes and robot embodiments. Project website with additional results and videos: https://nus-lins-lab.github.io/ObjectWorld/.

papers.title: Floquet-Parameterized Koopman-MPC for Tracking Periodic Orbits
papers.abstract: Designing real-time control for nonlinear systems to track periodic orbits can be challenging, especially for complex and coupled dynamical systems (e.g., tethered kites), where the true model parameters are hard to obtain. To address this, we propose a physics-informed Koopman learning approach that incorporates periodic-orbit stability directly into the learned linear predictor. The approach combines the underlying periodic structure of the dynamics along with periodic state-input trajectory data to learn physically consistent linear predictors (in lifted/observable space). We leverage Floquet theory, which studies the stability of periodic orbits in nonlinear systems, to obtain the periodic stability information of a given orbit via a monodromy matrix (i.e., the state transition matrix over an entire period). Subsequently, we impose open-loop monodromy constraints to learn Floquet-parameterized linear predictors using a least-squares Extended Dynamic Mode Decomposition (EDMD) formulation, thereby constraining the search space and aiding in Koopman learning. We then utilize these linear predictors to design a model predictive control (MPC) law for tracking periodic references. Finally, we evaluate the designed framework on a cartpole system under periodic forcing and compare it against a purely data-driven baseline.

papers.title: Enhancing Osteogenic Response in Selective Laser Melting-Fabricated Titanium through Hierarchical Micro/Nano Surface Engineering via Acid and Iodine Treatments
papers.abstract: Selective laser melting (SLM) enables the fabrication of patient-specific titanium (Ti) implants with complex geometries. However, the as-built SLM-Ti surfaces retain partially melted particles that may hinder favorable cellular responses. Because surface topography plays a critical role in regulating osteogenic cell behavior, controlled surface modification is needed to optimize these responses. In this study, SLM-Ti samples were treated with a mixed-acid solution for 1, 3, or 6 h (designated A1, A3, and A6, respectively) to regulate their macro- and microtopography. Surface characteristics were quantified using conventional roughness parameters (Ra and Rz) and fractal dimension (Df), which provided a quantitative measure of hierarchical surface complexity and guided surface optimization. The responses of MC3T3-E1 preosteoblasts to untreated and acid-treated samples were assessed by measuring cell proliferation, alkaline phosphatase (ALP) activity, and extracellular matrix mineralization. Among the acid-treated groups, A1 (Ra = 9.3 μm; Df = 1.187) showed the most favorable combination of cell proliferation and ALP activity, indicating enhanced early osteogenic differentiation. Accordingly, A1 was selected as the optimal macro-/microstructured surface for subsequent hierarchical modification. The A1 surface was then subjected to sequential NaOH-CaCl2-heat-ICl3 treatment to produce the A1-Io surface, which contained an iodine-containing calcium-deficient calcium titanate nanostructured layer superimposed on the microstructured surface. This hierarchical macro-/micro-/nanoarchitecture increased Df to 1.359, reflecting greater multiscale surface complexity. Compared with A1 alone, A1-Io enhanced late-stage extracellular matrix mineralization and further improved cell proliferation and ALP activity. These findings demonstrate that controlled acid etching followed by iodine treatment provides a quantitatively guided strategy for enhancing the osteogenic performance of SLM-fabricated titanium implants.

papers.title: Hydroxyapatite-Based Alendronate Coatings for Local Drug Delivery and Implant Osseointegration
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Hydroxyapatite (HA) coatings offer an osteoconductive interface and a mineral reservoir for alendronate. Their pharmaceutical value depends on whether binding produces biologically available exposure without impairing healing. This review examines that relationship in HA–alendronate coatings on titanium. Methods: A structured critical narrative review used PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus and Web of Science Core Collection, with reference-list screening. Screening identified 62 primary studies; contextual literature supported mechanistic and translational interpretation. Results: Adsorption, mineral incorporation, laser deposition and hybrid reservoirs produce different loading and release profiles. Cell and animal findings depend on formulation, dose, comparator and model. Mineral content, bone-to-implant contact and mechanical fixation provide complementary evidence and are not interchangeable outcomes. Human studies have mainly evaluated other bisphosphonates in fibrinogen coatings or alendronate applied as a gel around dental implants. Some reported less marginal bone loss, but improvements in implant stability were inconsistent. These results do not directly establish the efficacy of HA–alendronate coatings. Conclusions: Translation requires reproducible manufacture, measured active-drug availability, preserved physiological remodeling, durable coating adhesion and controlled trials for a defined implant indication. Strong mineral binding alone does not establish effective local therapy.

The Ta2O5-containing specimens exhibited lower roughness (3.4–5.0 versus 4.9–6.7 μm), higher hardness (226–239 versus 173 HV0.2), and lower water contact angles (31–33° versus 47°) than CP-Ti. EDS detected Ta and O, while XRD showed weak features consistent with retained Ta2O5. During SBF immersion, Ta2O5-containing specimens showed earlier deposits and greater apparent surface coverage, reaching 100% in analyzed SEM images after 28 days. SEM suggested more extensive MG-63 spreading and filopodial extension, particularly at 24 h. At 24 h, both Ta2O5-containing groups showed higher mean CCK-8 absorbance than CP-Ti, although between-group significance was not established. These findings indicate promising surface properties and early cellular responses, subject to differences in feedstock preparation and processing conditions.

A dense PEEK base supports a porous upper region containing a poly(vinyl alcohol)/poly(acrylic acid) (PVA/PAA) composite hydrogel. Sulfonation and ultraviolet-assisted acrylic acid (AA) treatment prepare the substrate for hydrogel attachment. At a 4:1 PVA:AA feed mass ratio, the drug-free composite construct (gPCH) exhibited a maximum detachment force per unit width of 304.60 ± 7.20 N m−1, 2.39 times that of PVA on sulfonated PEEK without AA/UV treatment. Its friction coefficient was 0.073 ± 0.005 during a 10 min screening test under 2 N in 25% fetal bovine serum at room temperature. The diclofenac sodium (DFN)-loaded counterpart (gPCHD) released 73.92 ± 3.24% of DFN over 72 h in PBS at 37 °C. In lipopolysaccharide-stimulated rabbit bone marrow-derived mesenchymal stem cells, gPCHD showed lower COX-1, COX-2, and IL-6 mRNA expression than composition-matched, drug-free gPCH. papers.title: Compressive Behavior and Energy Absorption of 3D ‐Printed Surface‐Modified TPMS Lattice Structures
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Triply periodic minimal surface (TPMS) based lattice structures have attracted considerable interest due to their high strength‐to‐weight ratio and adaptability for functional applications with their continuous topology. This paper presents a framework to generate TPMS lattice structures with tailored surface characteristics on Gyroid, Diamond, and Schwarz P lattices. Using mathematical modeling in MATLAB, rough and textured geometries are precisely constructed while maintaining structural continuity and periodicity. The standard and modified lattice structures were fabricated using fused deposition modeling (FDM) with acrylonitrile butadiene styrene (ABS) polymer. The performance of the fabricated lattice structures was evaluated under compression testing following the procedure outlined in ASTM D1621 to study the influence of surface modifications on deformation behavior and energy absorption of the fabricated lattice structures. Stress–strain response and failure behavior are analyzed, and the specific energy absorption is determined for nine TPMS lattices: three standard (Gyroid, Diamond, and Schwarz P), three modified with surface roughness, and three enhanced with textures. The surface modified with the roughness and texture configuration exhibited improved Young's modulus and specific energy absorption compared to standard Schwarz P TPMS structures.

papers.title: Predicting Soil Temperature and Quantifying Thermal Effects of Straw Mulching via a Data-Physics Dual-Driven Neural Network (Hy-PINN)
papers.abstract: Soil temperature is a critical meteorological factor influencing crop growth. Given that the dynamics of soil temperature under various straw mulching practices remain unclear, a two-year field experiment (2024–2025) was conducted. Four treatments were established—no mulching (CK), chopped straw mulching (CS), strip tillage (SS), and whole straw mulching (WS). Results indicated that straw mulching significantly altered the soil thermal environment; the cooling intensity followed the order of WS > SS > CS (averaging 0.58–1.72 °C) and was primarily concentrated during the seedling stage (1.09–2.82 °C). While full-scale mulching may induce early cold stress, SS mitigated this effect, providing a more balanced thermal environment. To address the reliance of traditional physical models on soil boundary conditions and parameters, we proposed a data-physics dual-driven hybrid physics-informed neural network (Hy-PINN). This model simultaneously predicts soil temperatures at 0 cm and 10 cm depths and dynamically inverts the apparent thermal diffusivity (κ). Through strict cross-year evaluation (training on 2024, independent testing on 2025), the Hy-PINN achieved high-precision predictions across all scenarios (R2 ≥ 0.89; RMSE ≤0.95 °C at 0 cm and ≤1.10 °C at 10 cm). The Hy-PINN model serves as a robust complementary tool to field monitoring, providing a scientific basis for assessing the thermal suitability of conservation tillage patterns.

papers.abstract: Electromagnetism is among the most conceptually demanding parts of the introductory university physics sequence, and it is also a field in which scientific communication (explaining invisible fields, justifying symmetry arguments, defending a solution to peers) is central to professional practice. Conventional lecture-and-problem-set instruction rarely develops these communicative skills systematically. This article proposes a methodological framework for teaching the Electromagnetism section of General Physics through Team-Based Learning (TBL) combined with peer instruction, case studies, jointly written laboratory reports and structured scientific debate. The framework operationalises communicative competence as five observable components (scientific language, argumentation, listening and questioning, collaboration, and scientific presentation), links each component to specific classroom activities, and provides a seven-module sequence from Coulomb's law to Maxwell's equations, together with an assessment rubric and a monitoring design based on concept inventories and the normalised gain. The paper is a design-oriented contribution grounded in the published evidence on active learning; empirical results of a pedagogical experiment are outside its scope and a protocol for such a study is provided.

papers.title: Robust Trajectory Planning Method for Complex Traffic Scenarios Based on Adversarial Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: Existing motion-planning methods for complex traffic suffer from imprecise vehicle-dynamics modeling and weak interaction with surrounding traffic participants, which limits safety and robustness. To address this, an adversary agent with an enlarged acceleration/steering action range is introduced to disturb the protagonist's safe driving, and the two agents are trained against each other within an adversarial reinforcement learning (RARL) framework without modifying the simulation environment; a hierarchical risk map evaluates road and obstacle risks, Gaussian process regression learns the residual uncertainty of the vehicle-dynamics model, and a model predictive controller fuses both to plan interaction-aware trajectories, while a multi-head network with adaptive action noise balances exploration and exploitation to accelerate convergence. Comparative experiments show that the adversarial strategy markedly improves comprehensive driving ability: under changes in speed, vehicle number and driving style, the proposed model achieves better safety, driving stability and efficiency than non-adversarial and conventional baselines.

papers.title: A Physics-Agnostic Tensor-Train Framework for Discretized Parametric Solution Maps of Dynamical Systems
papers.abstract: Wepresent a computational framework that builds the parametric solution map of a dynamical system as a family of tensor trains, one per state component, by cross-interpolation. A minimal contract separates the generic machinery from the specific dynamics: a physics module supplies the state derivative, the parameter axes with their ranges, and the index-to-state mapping, and nothing else changes between applications. Time is a tensor axis, so one integration fills a complete fiber for all state components; a bitwise-correct caching mechanism reduces the construction cost to one integration per distinct parameter point. We demonstrate the framework on a conservative cislunar problem, a dissipative atmospheric-flight problem, and a compartmental epidemic model, verified with instruments including an analytic vacuum limit, a nonlinear first integral, and a round-trip closure at least three orders below the reported errors. The construction attains a held-out accuracy of 3.6·10−7 at a compression factor of 8.9·105 on the first benchmark, of 6.6·10−4 at 7.8·102 on the second, and of 9.2·10−4 at 1.9·102 on the third. The rank rather than the grid is the binding constraint while the required rank stays below the grid cardinality, and the grid caps the attainable accuracy once it does not. The rank demand grows with the size of the uncertainty set and falls as it contracts: in the epidemic application, where every axis is a physical uncertainty, the rank falls to its minimum, while it plateaus in the other two applications. A comparison with polynomial chaos and Gaussian process surrogates on the same three families, under identical parameter boxes and error metrics, indicates that the difficulty of a parametric solution map is governed by the width of the parameter box direction by direction rather than by the number of directions.

papers.title: A Comprehensive Review of Leveraging Artificial Intelligence for CO 2 Emission Reduction Through Enhanced CCUS Design and Operation
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT The urgent need to decarbonize energy systems has heightened global focus on Carbon Capture, Utilization, and Storage (CCUS) technologies. This focus is particularly acute within OPEC countries, where hydrocarbon‐dependent economies face the dual challenge of reducing CO 2 emissions while preserving economic stability and global energy market relevance. Artificial Intelligence (AI) emerges as a transformative enabler, offering advanced methodologies—including machine learning, deep learning, reinforcement learning, Gaussian process regression, and fuzzy logic modelling—to optimize CCUS systems across multiple dimensions. This review systematically evaluates state‐of‐the‐art AI applications that improve CO 2 capture efficiency, optimize materials, predict storage behaviour, and enable real‐time leak detection. Furthermore, AI facilitates seamless integration of CCUS with renewable energy sources, supports intelligent decision‐making for utilization pathways such as enhanced oil recovery and synthetic fuel production, and advances techno‐economic optimization. Through critical analysis of recent studies, the review underscores AI's role in reducing the cost, uncertainty, and environmental impact of large‐scale CCUS deployment in hydrocarbon‐dependent economies, including OPEC member nations. Despite challenges related to data availability, computational demands, and model transparency, AI's potential to accelerate a low‐carbon energy transition remains compelling. The study recommends strategic policy and research priorities to promote AI‐driven innovation and sustainable climate action in hydrocarbon‐dependent economies.

It can be concluded that applying the Captain Ball game effectively enhances student activity and chest pass mastery in basketball learning.

This research employs a qualitative approach using a case study design, involving the school principal, PAI teachers, and supporting staff as the main informants. Data were collected through observation, in-depth interviews, and documentation, and analyzed using an interactive analysis model consisting of data reduction, data display, and conclusion drawing. Meanwhile, administrative supervision relates to the completeness of instructional documents, discipline, and the fulfillment of professional duties. This supervision has a positive impact on improving PAI teachers' performance, as shown by the improved quality of lesson documents, increased teaching method variations, and enhanced teacher professionalism. The study concludes that the school principal’s role as a supervisor is crucial in encouraging the improvement of PAI teacher performance. Structured, planned, and continuous supervision fosters a professional work environment and motivates teachers to enhance their competencies. Therefore, principal supervision serves as a vital instrument in improving the quality of Islamic Education learning in madrasah.
